title: Mating patterns
intro: Patterns that finish games: the smothered mate with its famous queen sacrifice, and the queen and bishop battery.

lessons.title: Smothered by its own pieces
lessons.summary: The knight mates a king that cannot move.

steps.text: The black king is surrounded by its own rook and pawns. It has no square to go to, so one knight check is enough.
Nf7 is checkmate. Nothing can take the knight, and a knight check cannot be blocked.

steps.hint: The king is smothered. Which knight jump gives check?
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Find the knight check.

steps.text: Often the corner is not closed yet. Then a queen sacrifice forces Black's own rook into the box: Qg8+! Rxg8, and the knight mates.
Play the famous combination: sacrifice the queen, then mate with the knight.
steps.hint: The queen checks on g8, where the king cannot take it because of your knight.
steps.ifWrong: Start with the queen sacrifice on g8.
steps.ifRight: Smothered mate! Black's own rook sealed the king in.

lessons.title: The queen and bishop battery
lessons.summary: Two pieces on one diagonal, aimed at the king.

steps.text: Your queen and bishop stand on the same long diagonal. Together they form a battery aimed at g7, and Black's g-pawn is gone.
Fire the battery: checkmate in one.
steps.hint: The queen can land on g7 or h8, protected by the bishop behind her.
steps.ifWrong: Not mate. Use the long diagonal: the bishop backs up your queen.
